Stella McCartney has been talking about animal rights at fashion week for 30 years. She is usually a lone voice, but the issue is back in the headlines this season. Outcry over the physical restraining of a Peta protester at a catwalk show by Steven Kolb, the president of New York fashion week’s governing body, has put cruelty in wool production – previously considered a niche issue compared with the hot button topic of fur – on the news agenda.

“There is no wool on the runway this season, and I’m proud of that,” McCartney said after her show. McCartney has been working on wool alternatives, including Brewed Protein, a fermented alternative to cashmere and wool developed in collaboration with the Japanese biotech firm Spiber, which was first used in her collections a year ago.

items.title: Federal Reserve watchdog finds no criminal violations for building renovation cost overruns
items.content_html:
Trump criticized $2.4bn rehab amid attempts to pressure then Fed chair Jerome Powell into lowering interest rates

The Federal Reserve’s internal watchdog said on Wednesday that the agency has broadly mismanaged an expansive building renovation project but did not find any criminal violations, as alleged by Trump administration prosecutors.

The Fed’s inspector general said that a variety of missteps by its board of governors inflated the cost of the $2.4bn renovation. The board did not secure a comprehensive cost estimate at the beginning of the project, nor did it nail down a maximum overall cost, a step that could have forced the building contractor to absorb the impact of inflation, the IG said in a 120-page report. Prices spiked after construction began in 2022.

items.title: What we know so far about alleged stabbing of pilot by co-pilot on flight to Israel
items.content_html:
Plane made emergency landing after pilot tried to crash aircraft, Israeli PM says, as officials investigate whether it was an attempted terror attack

One of the pilots of a plane flying from the UAE to Israel stabbed his co-pilot and appeared to try to crash the plane, the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, said, as Israeli officials said they were investigating whether the incident was an attempted terror attack on Israelis. Here is what we know so far:

A commercial plane travelling from Dubai in the United Arab Emirates to Israel was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia, after an apparent brawl between its pilots prompted distress signals that briefly raised fears of an attempted hijacking. The flydubai flight was over Jordan when it diverted to Saudi Arabia, transmitting three emergency signals, one of which indicated a possible unlawful interference.

The plane dipped dramatically during the reported fight, descending about 16,000ft in just two minutes. Israeli officials scrambled fighter jets, fearful of a possible hijacking attempt on a plane containing dozens of Israelis, and the plane landed at Tabuk airport in north-western Saudi Arabia.

Netanyahu said one of the flydubai pilots stabbed his co-pilot and appeared to be intending to crash the plane. He added that a passenger managed to break into the cockpit with one of the crew members, and together they “neutralised” the attacking pilot.

Netanyahu described it as “an extremely severe security incident”. Other officials, including the defence minister, Israel Katz, have called it an attempted terrorist attack. Netanyahu thanked the passengers and crew who helped to stop the attack, saying they “showed exceptional resourcefulness and courage”.

An Israeli official has identified the attacker as an Omani national, Reuters reported.

The Boeing 737 plane, which Israeli officials said had between 160 and 180 passengers onboard, transmitted a general emergency signal about two and a half hours after leaving Dubai, according to the flight-tracking website Flightradar24.

• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

As an Indian woman, I often feel myself oscillating between states of anxiety or anger. The anxiety is about doing the mental maths of how to stay safe – thinking about what I’m wearing, where I am going and how I’ll get there, and so on. The anger is at the sheer absurdity of this, and the stories of of sexual violence and harassment I read about every day. I am not the only one.

Last week, two particularly enraging incidents captured national attention. First, a video showing a group of men accused of harassing and molesting two teenagers at night in Bihar’s Jamui went viral. Then, a 17-year-old, out with a friend in Delhi, was allegedly gang-raped in a park by men posing as police. After, women in Bihar told Outlook how the incident in Jamui triggers greater controls and pressure on them. In Delhi, authorities curbed access to public parks and a premier women’s college, Lady Shri Ram College (LSR), briefly moved classes online.

items.title: Netanyahu et la victime perpétuelle
items.content_html:
Chaque mois de septembre, l'ONU rassemble les dirigeants du monde et répète ses lamentations sur l'effondrement d'un système fondé sur des règles. commande. Une règle n'est contraignante que dans la mesure où la transgresser devant les autres est embarrassant, là où Hannah Arendt a appelé l'espace d'apparence, où nous nous montrons tous aux autres, en dehors de la tribu, et acceptons d'être vus et jugés. Tant que ce lieu existait, les règles étaient discrètement violées. Aujourd'hui se Ils violent devant tout le monde, parce que personne ne parle devant les autres. Jeudi, cette défaite a pris la forme d’un soliloque. Alors que Netanyahu s'approchait du pupitre de l'Assemblée générale, des dizaines de délégations ont quitté la salle. Il a attendu que les murmures se calment et a invité tous les autres « lâches moraux » restés dans la pièce à partir. Plus que de déplorer le vide, il semblait le célébrer, comme quelqu'un qui sait qu'il ne parle pas au nom de ceux qui sont devant lui : Israël vote en octobre, et peu d'images conviennent mieux à Netanyahu que celle d'un dirigeant seul dans un monde hostile. Cette solitude lui a également servi à quelque chose de plus profond : garder pour lui toute la place de la victime.
